ordered_diagnoses: Primary Cutaneous Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma

facts.raw_span: A man in his 50s presented with a 12-year history of itchy eruptions over the whole body
Multiple nodules appeared on the upper back 1 year previously and gradually increased in number and size
extensive, dry scaly patches on the trunk, arms, and legs
Several 0.5- to 1-cm, dome-shaped, red papules and nodules were found on the upper back
Mildly enlarged lymph nodes were observed on the cervical, axillary, and inguinal regions
Routine blood tests, biochemistry analyses, and peripheral blood flow cytometry tests were within normal limits
No atypical cells were found in the peripheral blood
DNA analysis from paraffin sections showed clonal amplification product for the γ-chain of the T-cell receptor
Atrophy of the epidermis with focal orthokeratosis
Extensive, dense infiltrate of lymphocytes in the entire dermis
Small to medium-sized, atypical lymphocytes with focal areas of epidermotropism
Positive for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of itchy eruptions, skin lesions, and lymph node enlargement, along with the histopathological findings of atypical lymphocytes and epidermotropism, are consistent with Mycosis Fungoides, a type of cutaneous lymphoma.
The patient's presentation of extensive skin lesions, lymph node enlargement, and the presence of atypical lymphocytes in the skin, are consistent with Sezary Syndrome, a type of cutaneous lymphoma.
The patient's presentation of itchy eruptions and scaly patches on the skin, are consistent with Atopic Dermatitis, a type of inflammatory skin disease.
The patient's presentation of scaly patches and red papules on the skin, are consistent with Psoriasis, a type of inflammatory skin disease.

The patient's presentation of skin lesions and atypical lymphocytes, along with the absence of systemic symptoms, are consistent with Cutaneous Pseudolymphoma, a type of other dermatological condition.

The patient's presentation of skin lesions and atypical lymphocytes, along with the presence of lymph node enlargement, are consistent with Lymphomatoid Papulosis, a type of other dermatological condition.

rationales.F01: Itchy eruptions are common in various skin conditions, but the presence of nodules and lymphadenopathy suggests a more severe disease.
rationales.F02: The presence of nodules on the upper back is a distinctive feature of cutaneous lymphomas.
rationales.F04: Dome-shaped papules and nodules are characteristic of cutaneous lymphomas, particularly Mycosis Fungoides.
rationales.F08: Clonal amplification of the T-cell receptor gamma chain is a hallmark of T-cell lymphomas.
rationales.F11: Atypical lymphocytes with epidermotropism are characteristic of Mycosis Fungoides and other cutaneous T-cell lymphomas.
rationales.F12: Immunohistochemical staining positive for CD2, CD3, CD4, and CD45RO is consistent with a T-cell lymphoma, particularly Mycosis Fungoides.
